title: The Tale of Chunhyang
note: A concise reading-copy retelling following the public-domain “Chun Yang, The Faithful Dancing-Girl Wife.” It is one interpretation of the much-retold Chunhyang tradition, not an authoritative text of the pansori cycle.

rights.basis: The 1889 English collection is identified as public domain in the United States by Project Gutenberg. This concise reading copy is newly written for the collection.

artLabel: Chunhyang and Mongryong meet beside the flowering pavilion at Gwanghallu in Namwon.

pageArt.alt: Chunhyang refuses the corrupt magistrate before his court in Namwon.
Mongryong reveals his royal inspector’s seal and reunites with Chunhyang after justice is restored.

scenes: In Namwon lived Yi Mongryong, the young son of the district magistrate. One spring day he visited the pavilion of Gwanghallu and saw Chunhyang riding on a swing among the flowering trees.

Chunhyang was the daughter of Wolmae, once a court entertainer. She was admired for her learning as well as her beauty. Mongryong sent his servant to ask her name, and before long the two young people pledged themselves to one another.

Their happiness was brief. Mongryong’s father was recalled to the capital, and the son had to leave with his family. He promised Chunhyang that he would return after completing the state examinations.

A new magistrate came to Namwon. Hearing of Chunhyang, he ordered her to entertain him. She refused, saying that she had already pledged her heart and would not betray it. Furious, the magistrate had her beaten and imprisoned.

In the capital, Mongryong passed his examinations and was appointed a secret royal inspector. Disguised in worn clothes, he traveled through the province to discover how its officials treated the people.

He returned to Namwon looking like a penniless wanderer. Even when Chunhyang heard that he seemed poor, she did not withdraw her love. Meanwhile the magistrate prepared a lavish birthday feast while prisoners and villagers suffered.
At the height of the feast, Mongryong’s agents surrounded the court. He revealed the royal inspector’s seal, dismissed the corrupt magistrate, and ordered Chunhyang released.
Chunhyang and Mongryong were reunited, and her courage was honored before the province.
